item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q007_chey_like_function_divergence","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 supports remote evolutionary homology at the superfamily level: all three belong to the CheY-like superfamily c.23.1 within the Flavodoxin-like fold c.23. They are separate families—CheY-related response regulators c.23.1.1 (SUNID 52173), the ornithine-decarboxylase N-terminal “wing” c.23.1.4 (SUNID 52252), and the KaiA N-terminal domain c.23.1.5 (SUNID 82344)—so the classification does not establish close family-level equivalence. In particular, it does not show that the ODC wing or KaiA N-terminal domain is a canonical CheY-like phosphoaccepting response regulator or participates in two-component phosphotransfer; nor does it imply that CheY-related proteins or KaiA bind PLP or catalyze ornithine decarboxylation. The ODC wing’s classification alone also cannot assign decarboxylase activity independently of the intact enzyme and its active-site context. Cross-family members may serve as remote topology templates, but not as functional templates or interchangeable representatives. Such transfers require family-proximal sequence and domain-architecture evidence, conservation of relevant phosphoacceptor or catalytic/cofactor-binding residues, ligand-bound structural evidence, and direct phosphotransfer, KaiA interaction/circadian-function, or PLP-dependent decarboxylase assays as appropriate.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_node — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.23","mcp__scope__get_scop_node — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.23.1","mcp__scope__list_scop_children — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/52172/children?limit=20","mcp__scope__list_scop_children — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/52173/children?limit=20"]}]}
